To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 1.3 μm RS-BH DFB laser with an asymmetric corrugation pitch modulation (ACPM) grating can be used to realize a cost-effective light-source for 400 Gb/s optical transmission systems.
the 1.3-$\mu $ m InAlGaAs RS-BH ACPM DFB lasers are the first to demonstrate successful 56-Gb/s and 50-Gb-s transmission over 10-km SMFs.

the combination of low-leakage ridge-shaped-burried heterostructure and asymmetric corrugation pitch modulation grating is effective to achieve direct modulation at 56 Gbit/s and 50 Gbit/s for back-to-back operation and 56 Gbit and 50 Gbits/s over 10-km SMF for 400 Gb/s and OTU5 application.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, fabrication and characterization of 1.55-μm InP-based distributed Bragg reflector (DBR) lasers for use as light sources in 100 Gb/s and beyond applications.
the design and fabrication of InP-based DFB lasers.

the design and fabrication of a new type of DFB lasers, which are suitable for use as a light source for 400 Gb/s applications, and the demonstration of direct modulation at a bit rate of 56 Gb s-1 at 55 °C.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RS-BH DFB laser has been demonstrated to have the potential to be a viable candidate for use as a 400 Gb/s light source in 100 GbE, OTU3, and 400 Gb E applications.
we have developed a novel type of DFB laser with superior properties that enables direct modulation at 56 Gbit/s and 55 °C, and 50 Gbit/s at up to +80 °C, with clear eye opening.
the results presented in this work demonstrate the potential of the RS-BH DFB lasers for 56 and 55°C, and 50 Gbps and 80°C direct modulation, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully demonstrated the first 50 GbE and 50 Gbps OTU5 transceiver using InGaAlAs RS-BH DFB lasers.
we developed the 1.3 μm DFB lasers that are capable of running at 56 and even 50 Gb/sec at up to 55°C and even 80°C.

we have developed 1.3 $\mu$ m InGaAlas ridge shaped buried heterostructure distributed feedback lasers with 56 Gb/sec direct modulation and transmission over a 10 km single mode fiber at 85°C and 55°C, which are the highest data rates reported to date for a 1.3$\mu$m laser.
The main takeaway from our work is that
this type of laser is suitable for high-speed direct modulation.
the combination of the ACPM grates with the RS-BH structure is a promising approach for realizing low-cost, low-leakage lasers with excellent direct modulation performance.
the RS-BH structure is a promising candidate for realizing high-speed, low-cost lasers for 400 Gb/s and beyond.
